court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Shikohabad, District-Firozabad, Case No.138 of 2023
case_name: Ashwani Kumar Yadav And 7 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ashwani Kumar Yadav and 7 others (husband, wife, etc.)

facts_of_case: The FIR was lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicants under Sections 494, 504, 506, 120B IPC with allegations of torture and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: To constitute an offence under Section 494 IPC, it is necessary that the Saptapadi ceremony (taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire) is one of the essential ingredients of a valid marriage under Hindu law.
legal_principles.held: It is well settled that to constitute an offence under Section 494 IPC, it is necessary that the Saptapadi ceremony ((taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire)) is one of the essential ingredients of a valid marriage under Hindu law.
cited_cases: Smriti Singh Alias Mausami Singh and 3 Others vs. State of U.P. and another (Application U/s 482 No.23148 of 2022, decided on 19.09.2023)

legal_principles.principle: Ceremonies in the Hindu Marriage is said to be performed when 'Saptapadi', i.e. taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire.
legal_principles.held: Specifying Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, he submits that ceremonies in the Hindu Marriage is said to be performed when 'Saptapadi', i.e. taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire.

outcome.final_order: The charge-sheet dated 31.12.2023 and cognizance/summoning order dated 15.06.2024 were quashed.
